description: Cosmophiles is a team passionate about astronomy, astrophysics, and exploring the mysteries of our universe. We’re tackling NASA’s Planet X and SPHEREx challenge by developing an interactive tool to explore astronomical observations and investigate celestial objects that move or change over time. We’re looking for curious minds, especially web developers (HTML, CSS, JavaScript), Python developers, and astronomy enthusiasts. Let’s learn, collaborate, and build something meaningful together!
summary: COSMOSCOPE is an interactive astronomical exploration prototype developed by Team Cosmophiles for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge. It combines an accessible project interface with an interactive celestial sky viewer powered by CDS Aladin Lite, allowing users to explore the sky through astronomical coordinates and survey visualization. The current prototype establishes the foundation for future integration of genuine SPHEREx observations, target-specific investigation, and multi-epoch comparisons. Simulated interface visuals are clearly distinguished from actual astronomical observations.
details:
COSMOSCOPE is an interactive astronomical exploration prototype developed by Team Cosmophiles for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

The prototype features a designed exploration interface and an interactive celestial sky viewer powered by CDS Aladin Lite. Users can navigate astronomical sky visualizations and explore celestial coordinates and available sky surveys.

The project aims to make astronomical exploration more accessible and establish a foundation for future integration of genuine SPHEREx observations, target investigation, and multi-epoch comparison.

The current prototype does not yet retrieve SPHEREx observations directly. Its generated target visuals are illustrative, not scientific measurements.
